member.name: CandidateRuntimeIdentifiers
member.para: Why the fallback is guesswork rather than a measurement. The macOS branch was written 2026-08-22 without a Mac to run it on, and the project deliberately ships no macOS binaries and added no CI, so nothing here has ever observed what returns on Apple Silicon. The concern is inherited from .NET Core's portable-RID era, where a runtime built against a specific macOS release reported a version-stamped identifier; with an explicit -r osx-arm64 publish it should report exactly that RID, and on this project's own two platforms it demonstrably does. The second candidate is therefore expected to be dead code on every machine anyone here can check. It stays because the cost of being wrong is asymmetric: the failure is not "no GPU acceleration", it is the Silero load throwing and the run ending.

What the publish layout actually looks like, cross-published from Windows and listed 2026-08-22 at Whisper.net 1.9.1 / Microsoft.ML.OnnxRuntime 1.27.1. macOS is the one target where the two native trees disagree about the folder name, so both spellings appear side by side: Whisper's dylibs land in runtimes/macos-arm64/ and the ONNX dylib in runtimes/osx-arm64/. Only the second is this resolver's business - Whisper.net probes for its own by a mechanism of its own - which is why the naming trap costs nothing here and has to be handled in the csproj instead.

The Intel Mac is not merely untested. Microsoft.ML.OnnxRuntime 1.27.1 ships android, ios, linux-arm64, linux-x64, osx-arm64, win-arm64 and win-x64, and no osx-x64 at all. No ONNX Runtime means no Silero, and since 0.12.0 the VAD pre-pass runs on every file with a load failure being fatal rather than a degradation - so on an Intel Mac the tool would not run at all rather than run without jingle geometry.

osx-arm64 has no providers_shared native, unlike every other platform in the package: runtimes/osx-arm64/native/ holds libonnxruntime.dylib and nothing else. That is why the csproj's move step names one file on macOS and two everywhere else, and why this resolver's "onnxruntime itself loads its companion from its own directory" reasoning has nothing to load there.
